label: leadership development and partner management
overview: Leadership development in a professional services firm operates across two distinct dimensions: developing the next generation of leaders through a structured promotion pathway, and managing the conduct and culture of the existing leadership group. The most common failure in CA and advisory firm leadership is promoting technically excellent practitioners into leadership roles without assessing their leadership capability — creating leaders who are brilliant at the work but ineffective at developing people, managing conduct, and making partnership-level decisions. A rigorous promotion checklist, a conduct management framework, and the use of personality profiling tools (particularly the Enneagram) together provide a comprehensive approach to building and sustaining a high-quality leadership culture.

diagnostic_entry.primary_question: Is the leadership challenge primarily about developing and promoting the next generation of leaders, managing conduct or performance issues within the existing leadership group, building self-awareness and communication effectiveness across the team, or maintaining ethical standards and accountability?
diagnostic_entry.leadership_pipeline: When the firm's leadership pipeline is thin — when there are no credible internal succession candidates for partner or management roles — the intervention requires a structured development pathway, not just a promotion checklist. The checklist defines the destination; the development pathway defines how candidates get there.
diagnostic_entry.conduct_management: When an existing leader is behaving in ways that are inconsistent with the firm's values or performance expectations, a structured conduct management process is required. The process must be evidence-based, consistently applied, and separated from personality conflicts — which are the most common source of conduct management failures.
diagnostic_entry.self_awareness_and_communication: When leadership effectiveness is being undermined by interpersonal friction, communication breakdowns, or leadership style mismatches, personality profiling provides the shared language and framework for productive conversations. The Enneagram is particularly effective in professional services contexts because it addresses motivational drivers, not just behavioural patterns.
diagnostic_entry.ethical_standards: When conduct issues involve professional ethics, the intervention must be both developmental and consequential. A demerit system provides a graduated, transparent, and consistent accountability mechanism that treats ethics breaches seriously without defaulting immediately to dismissal for first-time or minor infractions.

support_tools.name: Partner Promotion Checklist
support_tools.purpose: Provides a structured, evidence-based framework for evaluating whether a candidate is genuinely ready for partnership — assessing capability across the four dimensions that determine partner-level success in a professional services firm.
support_tools.core_principle: The most costly leadership mistake in a CA or advisory firm is promoting someone to partner who is not ready. The cost is not just the underperformance of the promoted individual — it is the signal it sends to the rest of the team about what the firm values, and the difficulty of managing down someone who has already received the public recognition of a promotion.
support_tools.when_to_use: Use for all partner or principal admission decisions — both internal promotions and external lateral hires at the partner level.

four_dimensions.description: Has demonstrated consistent expert-level judgement in their technical domain. Handles the most complex client scenarios independently. Is recognised by peers, clients, and professional networks as a technical authority.
evidence_required: Examples of complex technical matters resolved independently
Client feedback or NPS data that specifically references technical quality
Peer review scores or quality assessment results
CPD record and any specialist qualifications obtained

four_dimensions.description: Has a defined portfolio of clients whose primary relationship is with the candidate — clients who trust the individual, not just the firm brand, and who would follow the candidate in a lateral move.
evidence_required: Client retention data for the candidate's portfolio over 3+ years
Revenue growth in existing client relationships attributable to the candidate
Testimonials or references from key clients
Evidence of the candidate navigating difficult client conversations independently

four_dimensions.description: Has a track record of generating new client revenue — not just servicing what exists. Understands and accepts that partnership requires consistent contribution to firm growth, not just delivery excellence.
evidence_required: New client revenue generated in the preceding 24 months (name and revenue)
Pipeline of identified business development opportunities with a credible action plan
Referral network development — COI relationships maintained and producing referrals
Evidence of speaking, writing, or thought leadership that creates inbound enquiries

four_dimensions.description: Demonstrates the capacity to build and develop the capabilities of others — not just manage tasks. Has evidence of staff developing and being promoted under their supervision.
evidence_required: Staff who have been promoted or significantly developed under their direct supervision
Evidence of coaching or mentoring activity beyond task management
Handling of at least one difficult people management situation with a documented positive outcome

scoring_and_decision.approach: Score each dimension independently using a 1-5 scale with defined descriptors for each level. A candidate must achieve a minimum of 3 in all four dimensions and an average of 4 across the four to be considered promotion-ready.
red_lines: A score of 1 or 2 in any dimension is a disqualifier — regardless of scores in other dimensions
Business development score of 2 or below disqualifies regardless of technical excellence
A candidate who has not had a people management responsibility should not be admitted to partnership in a people-management role

support_tools.name: Conduct Management Framework
support_tools.purpose: Provides a structured, evidence-based, and legally defensible process for managing conduct issues within the leadership group — ensuring that conduct concerns are addressed consistently, documented thoroughly, and escalated proportionately.
support_tools.core_principle: Conduct management fails most often because it is inconsistent. When conduct standards are applied rigorously to some individuals and ignored for others — particularly senior individuals — the firm's culture interprets this as evidence that the standards are aspirational, not real. Consistent application, even when uncomfortable at the senior level, is the only way to make conduct standards credible.
support_tools.when_to_use: Use when a leader's behaviour is creating documented harm — to team members, client relationships, or the firm's reputation — and informal conversation has not produced a change in behaviour.

conduct_categories.description: Failure to meet agreed performance standards — billing targets, client retention, people management obligations. Managed through the Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) framework.
conduct_categories.process: Refer to the PIP framework in the fm-coach-culture domain.

conduct_categories.description: Behaviour that is inconsistent with the firm's stated values — including aggressive communication, disrespect of team members, failure to maintain confidentiality, or conduct that creates a hostile working environment.
conduct_categories.process: Document specific instances with evidence. Conduct a formal meeting with the individual, a support person present if requested, and a partner or HR representative. State the specific behaviour, the standard required, and the support available. Document the outcome and review at an agreed date.

conduct_categories.description: Conduct that affects the firm's professional obligations — including errors in professional judgement, failure to comply with compliance standards, or conduct that creates regulatory or legal risk for the firm.
conduct_categories.process: Engage the firm's professional indemnity insurer and legal advisor before taking any action. Professional conduct issues have consequences beyond the individual that require specific expertise to manage.

progressive_discipline_sequence.action: Informal conversation — documented by the manager but not placed on file. Purpose is to make the individual aware of the concern and create an opportunity to self-correct.
Formal verbal warning — documented and placed on file. Specific behaviour described, standard required stated, improvement period and consequences of recurrence both defined.
Written warning — formal letter documenting the breach, prior warnings, the required improvement, and the consequence of a further breach.
Final written warning or suspension — used for serious or repeated breaches. Requires HR or legal review before issuing.
Termination — requires legal advice and, in the case of a partner, review of the partnership agreement. Never proceed without documented evidence at all prior levels.

support_tools.name: Enneagram Leadership Profiling
support_tools.purpose: Provides a personality profiling framework tailored to professional services leadership contexts — creating shared language for leadership team communication, identifying leadership style strengths and blind spots, and improving the quality of interpersonal dynamics within the partnership.
support_tools.core_principle: The Enneagram is particularly valuable in leadership contexts because it addresses motivational drivers — why people behave as they do under stress — rather than simply describing observable behaviour. In a partnership where leadership style clashes and communication breakdowns are common sources of dysfunction, understanding the motivational drivers behind each partner's behaviour is more useful than surface-level communication style analysis.
support_tools.when_to_use: Use when leadership team dynamics are creating friction, when communication between partners is frequently misunderstood or misinterpreted, or when preparing a new partner for the interpersonal complexity of a partnership environment.

nine_types_overview.name: The Reformer
nine_types_overview.core_motivation: To be good, ethical, and right. Fears being corrupt or wrong.

nine_types_overview.name: The Helper
nine_types_overview.core_motivation: To be needed and appreciated. Fears being unwanted or unloved.
nine_types_overview.leadership_blind_spot: Struggles with saying no, may enable underperformance to preserve relationships
nine_types_overview.under_stress: Becomes manipulative and resentful when needs are unmet

nine_types_overview.name: The Achiever
nine_types_overview.core_motivation: To be successful and admired. Fears failure and being worthless.
nine_types_overview.leadership_blind_spot: May cut corners for results, struggles with vulnerability
nine_types_overview.under_stress: Becomes deceptive about difficulties to maintain image

nine_types_overview.name: The Individualist
nine_types_overview.core_motivation: To be unique and authentic. Fears having no personal significance.
nine_types_overview.leadership_strength: Creative, emotionally perceptive, brings distinctive perspective
nine_types_overview.leadership_blind_spot: May become withdrawn or dramatic, struggles with team conformity

nine_types_overview.name: The Investigator
nine_types_overview.core_motivation: To be capable and knowledgeable. Fears being useless or incompetent.
nine_types_overview.leadership_blind_spot: Withdraws from team engagement, over-analyzes before deciding

nine_types_overview.name: The Loyalist
nine_types_overview.core_motivation: To have security and support. Fears being without guidance or support.
nine_types_overview.leadership_blind_spot: Anxiety-prone, may create worst-case scenarios, struggles with authority

nine_types_overview.name: The Enthusiast
nine_types_overview.core_motivation: To be happy and avoid pain. Fears being deprived or in pain.
nine_types_overview.leadership_blind_spot: Struggles to follow through, avoids difficult conversations

nine_types_overview.name: The Challenger
nine_types_overview.core_motivation: To be self-reliant and in control. Fears being controlled or harmed.
nine_types_overview.leadership_blind_spot: Confrontational, struggles with delegating control, can intimidate

nine_types_overview.name: The Peacemaker
nine_types_overview.core_motivation: To have peace and harmony. Fears conflict and loss of connection.
nine_types_overview.leadership_strength: Mediating, inclusive, able to see all perspectives
nine_types_overview.leadership_blind_spot: Conflict-avoidant, may fail to take a clear position when required

application_in_leadership_teams.partnership_dynamics: In a CA firm partnership, the most common destructive pairing is a Type 8 (Challenger) partner who makes decisions unilaterally paired with a Type 9 (Peacemaker) partner who avoids raising concerns. The Enneagram framework creates the language for the Type 9 to name the dynamic and the Type 8 to understand the impact of their style.
application_in_leadership_teams.client_communication: Understanding a client's Enneagram type enables the advisor to tailor their communication style — a Type 1 client needs precision and evidence; a Type 3 client needs to see results and status; a Type 5 client needs depth and space to process.
application_in_leadership_teams.team_composition: A leadership team dominated by a single type or cluster of types has identifiable blind spots. A team of all Type 5s will over-analyse and under-act. A team of all Type 3s will move fast but may miss risk. Profiling the team creates awareness of collective blind spots that no individual audit would reveal.

support_tools.name: Ethics Demerit System
support_tools.purpose: Provides a graduated, transparent, and consistently applied accountability mechanism for ethics breaches within the firm — ensuring that professional ethics standards are treated as real, enforceable commitments rather than aspirational statements.
support_tools.core_principle: An ethics standard that is never enforced is not a standard — it is a suggestion. The demerit system provides graduated consequences that are proportionate to the severity of the breach, transparent to all partners, and consistently applied regardless of seniority. Its value is not primarily punitive — it is the signal it sends about the firm's genuine commitment to its stated values.
support_tools.when_to_use: Use as part of the firm's governance framework when establishing or refreshing ethics standards, when an ethics breach has occurred that requires a structured response, or when the firm is preparing for a merger or external quality audit.

examples: Failure to complete CPD requirements by the due date
Late submission of regulatory filings where no client harm resulted
Use of firm resources for minor personal purposes without authorisation
breach_categories.consequence: Formal notation in the partner's file. Discussion at the next partner review meeting. No financial penalty unless repeated.

examples: Providing advice outside the scope of the firm's professional indemnity coverage without disclosure
Failure to manage a conflict of interest appropriately after it was identified
Misrepresentation of qualifications or experience to a client
breach_categories.consequence: Written warning. Mandatory remediation training or supervision for a defined period. Financial penalty equivalent to one month's profit distribution if the breach is repeated within 12 months.

examples: Client funds used for unauthorised purposes
Deliberate suppression of information material to a client's decision
Conduct that brings the firm into serious professional or public disrepute
breach_categories.consequence: Suspension pending investigation. Engagement of legal and professional indemnity advisors. Potential referral to the professional regulatory body. If upheld, termination of the partnership agreement.

demerit_threshold_and_consequences.accumulation: Demerit points accumulate over a rolling 36-month period. Points from more than 36 months ago are no longer active.

thresholds.consequence: Mandatory review meeting with the managing partner and a written improvement plan
Formal disciplinary review. Reduction in profit share by 10% for 6 months.
Final warning and 6-month probationary period. Reduction in profit share by 25%.
Exit from the partnership — processes governed by the partnership agreement.

governance_requirements: The demerit register must be maintained by an independent partner or an external governance advisor — not the managing partner, who may have a conflict of interest
All partners must have access to the categories, point allocations, and thresholds — the system cannot operate as a surprise
Any partner who believes a demerit has been wrongly applied has 14 days to formally contest the decision through the firm's dispute resolution process
The demerit register is reviewed annually as part of the partnership governance cycle

support_tools.name: Leadership Development — If-Then Guidance
support_tools.purpose: Decision logic for the most common leadership development complications — failed promotions, conduct management resistance, Enneagram misuse, and ethics breach escalation.

if_then_logic.condition: A promotion candidate meets three of four dimensions on the checklist but is significantly below target on business development
if_then_logic.action: Do not promote. Business development is a non-negotiable partnership dimension — a partner who cannot generate new revenue is a cost to the remaining partners' growth capacity. Design an 18-24 month development plan with specific, measurable business development milestones. Re-evaluate against the full checklist when the milestones have been met.

if_then_logic.condition: A senior partner is resistant to the conduct management process and claims the standards do not apply at their level
if_then_logic.action: This response is itself a conduct issue. The managing partner must address the resistance directly and immediately — partner-level exemption from conduct standards is one of the most corrosive messages a firm can send to its team. If the managing partner is unable to hold the standard with the senior partner, engage an external advisor to facilitate the conversation.

if_then_logic.condition: An Enneagram profiling session creates conflict rather than understanding between partners
if_then_logic.action: Stop the session. Enneagram profiling can amplify existing interpersonal tensions if the facilitator does not have sufficient experience with high-conflict professional groups. Debrief individually before bringing the group back together. The individual debrief conversations reveal whether the conflict is about the profiling content or is a pre-existing relationship issue using the profiling session as a proxy battleground.

if_then_logic.condition: A Serious Breach (10 demerit points) is contested by the partner involved
if_then_logic.action: Activate the formal dispute resolution process immediately. Engage the firm's external legal advisor before taking any further action. Do not suspend without legal advice — an unlawful suspension creates greater liability than the underlying breach. Document every action and communication from the point the breach was identified.

advisor_guidance.promotion_decisions_are_culture_signals: Every promotion decision in a professional services firm is read by the entire team as a signal of what the firm actually values — not what it says it values. A promotion of a technically excellent but relationship-poor partner sends the message that relationship skills are optional. Use the checklist consistently, and when candidates fall short of it, be explicit about why and what the development pathway is.
advisor_guidance.conduct_management_at_senior_level_requi: The most important conduct management interventions are at the most senior levels, where the cultural impact is greatest. The most common failure is allowing poor conduct at the partner level to persist because the managing partner is conflict-averse, or because the conduct is being tolerated in exchange for the individual's financial contribution. Financial contribution does not exempt any individual from the firm's conduct standards.
advisor_guidance.enneagram_is_a_tool_not_a_label: The Enneagram's value in leadership contexts is creating self-awareness and mutual understanding — not providing a categorisation that excuses behaviour. A Type 8 partner who is consistently aggressive cannot attribute their behaviour to their type. The type provides the language for understanding the motivation; the leader is still responsible for managing the behaviour. Use the profiling to open conversations, not to close them.
advisor_guidance.ethics_systems_only_work_if_applied_cons: A demerit system that is applied rigorously to junior partners and inconsistently to senior partners is worse than no system at all — it creates resentment and signals that the firm's ethics standards are performative. Before implementing the demerit system, the managing partner must be genuinely prepared to apply it at all levels of the partnership, including to themselves.
